A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KOWCPI research and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–E. Their equations, tables, figures, and proofs support reliable comparison despite the changed title and pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original coverage and interval-width experiments on electricity, wind, solar, AAPL stock prices, and synthetic time series in Section 5 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the real-data comparisons, synthetic simulations, and adaptive-window experiment.

M1.justification: The RNW weighting procedure, residual-block construction, quantile estimation, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The multivariate extension in Appendix A and adaptive window selection in Appendix E already appear in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same electricity, wind, solar, and AAPL datasets, along with the same heteroskedastic-mixture and nonstationary synthetic scenarios. No evaluated task or population is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Plain NW, SPCI, EnbPI, ACI, FACI, AgACI, SF-OGD, SAOCP, and SCP. Tables A.1–A.3 also preserve their corresponding comparator sets.

E3.justification: The 7:1:2 main-data split, AAPL 80/20 split, 10-tree random forest, 90% coverage target, evaluation metrics, tuning procedures, and synthetic data-generating settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the Plain NW comparison, rolling-coverage analyses, Solar interval case study, synthetic robustness tests, and fixed-versus-adaptive window comparison. None of these analyses is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both report standard deviations across five trials in Tables 1, A.3, and A.4, three trials in Table A.1, and results for five simulated paths in Table A.2. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1 and A.1–A.4 and the plotted results match. For example, Table 1 retains KOWCPI widths of 0.22, 2.41, and 48.8 for Electric, Wind, and Solar, respectively, with the same coverage values and standard deviations.

T1.justification: The marginal coverage bound, Assumptions 4.2–4.5, consistency and conditional coverage results, Appendix A's multivariate definitions, and Appendix B's proofs are unchanged. Equation reflow does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive weights, coverage guarantees, and narrower prediction intervals. Adding time-series wording to the title makes the existing scope explicit.

C2.justification: The explanation involving greater weights on recent residuals, qualification about brief coverage failures from rapid adaptation, residual-mixing discussion, and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both provide the same implementation and tuning details, baseline-code access links, AAPL data link, synthetic model specifications, and adaptive-window KS-test threshold. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list retain the same works and research positioning. Reference pagination changes without substantive bibliographic additions or removals.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Kernel-based Optimally Weighted Conformal Prediction Intervals' to 'Kernel-based Optimally Weighted Conformal Time-Series Prediction.' Section 5 also corrects 'eletric' to 'electric'; the narrative and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title now occupies two lines, and text and equations reflow across pages and around existing figures, tables, and Algorithm 1. Figure images, captions, and table structures remain unchanged, with no added or removed displays.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the title's time-series focus and corrects a spelling error, while retaining the same method, theory, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information. These small editorial changes and pagination shifts do not produce a meaningful overall quality gain or decline.
